title: Spectral Analysis Lab: Robot-Assisted Light Dispersion
description: A robot lab assistant helps you perform a spectral analysis experiment. The user wears virtual safety sunglasses, activates a dispersion prism to split white light into its component wavelengths, then instructs the robot to collect and identify each spectral band by clicking on colored beams. The goal is to correctly label all visible spectrum wavelengths in order.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements an interactive chemistry spectral analysis lab. Load three GLB assets: SunglassesKhronos.glb (safety glasses), DispersionTest.glb (a prism/dispersion model), and robot.glb (a lab assistant robot). Set up a dark laboratory scene with a black background and subtle ambient light (intensity 0.3) plus one white directional light simulating a light source aimed at the dispersion model. Position the camera at (0, 2, 6) looking at the origin. Place the dispersion prism model at center (0, 1, 0), the robot to the right at (3, 0, 0) facing the prism, and the sunglasses floating near the camera at (-1, 2.5, 3). Interaction steps: Step 1 - User clicks the sunglasses to 'put them on', which attaches them to the camera and adds a subtle tinted post-processing overlay (a semi-transparent colored plane in front of the camera). Step 2 - User clicks a 'Power On' HTML button to activate the light source, increasing directional light intensity to 2.0 and creating 7 colored line segments (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet) emanating from the prism model to simulate spectral dispersion using THREE.Line with vertex colors. Step 3 - User clicks on individual spectral beams (raycasting on the colored lines). When a beam is clicked, the robot animates (play its first animation clip) and moves toward that beam using a simple tween over 1 second. Step 4 - A floating HTML label appears near the clicked beam showing the wavelength range (e.g., 'Red: 620-750nm'). Track which beams have been identified. Step 5 - After all 7 beams are clicked and labeled, display a congratulatory overlay saying 'Spectral Analysis Complete' with a summary table of all wavelengths. Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation. Add a subtle grid helper on the floor. Ensure all models are scaled appropriately (auto-scale each to fit within a 2-unit bounding box).
